premise: I cashed out my $131,000 401(k) to become a 45% partner in my son’s solar‑panel installation company, notarizing a lifetime of free electricity for my home; after a green‑energy firm offered $790,000 for the contracts, he forged a dissolution, sold my stake, and mailed me a $4,800 “utility bill” credit—I retrieved our original partnership agreement sealed inside the wiring diagram of a solar inverter, voided the sale, and now own “Watt of Deceit Solar,” where he cleans panels in a vest that says “Short‑Circuited Trust” and every installation manual prints his fraud‑docket number.
